extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and research administrators preparing NIH NRSA F31 (pre-doctoral) grant application materials (biosketch, facilities & resources, senior/key person profile)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for sections of an NIH NRSA F31 pre-doctoral fellowship application, including Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment descriptions, Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) fields, and the Biographical Sketch format and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe laboratory and office space, equipment, dedicated rooms, and institutional support relevant to the proposed research (e.g., recently renovated laboratory space on the third floor of the Rollins Research Center; standard wet benches, certified fume hood, sink, utilities, deionized water; adjoining room dedicated for cell culture; percent use of cold room and freezer room; all equipment required is housed within the laboratory). Note biosafety approvals (e.g., approved for Biosafety Level 2 (BSL-2) work with current biosafety approvals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include square footage, specific dedicated rooms, percent/shared use of specialized spaces, immediate proximity to cores/other labs (walking times), and explicit statement of biosafety level and approvals. Provide enough detail to demonstrate that the environment and resources are adequate for the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer resources (within Facilities & Other Resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: List computing hardware, software, network access, and shared computational facilities (e.g., Apple MacBook Pro loaded with Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop, Endnote, Findings electronic notebook; wireless Internet access throughout lab and office; access to a departmental server with a backup system; laboratory and office networked computers and printers; dedicated molecular graphics area with 2 x Apple Mac OSX workstations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify software packages, data processing/model-building workstations, backup systems, and any shared visualization/graphics resources that support the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support: X-ray Crystallographic Facilities & Synchrotron access
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe departmental/state-of-the-art core facilities supporting the project (e.g., ~150 sq. ft. automated crystallization and in-house X-ray data collection facility; Emory membership in SER-CAT at the Advanced Photon Source providing 12 days ID beamtime and 12 days BM beamtime per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State facility size, purpose, which research groups they support, beamtime or external access allocations (days/year), and reference attached letters or equipment sections for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conn Laboratory — Equipment availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail major equipment and instrumentation available in the sponsor's laboratory to perform the proposed work (examples listed: Infors Multitron dual and Ecotron orbital shaker incubators with cooling module; Beckman Allegra 25R centrifuge; ÄKTA Purifier10 FPLC systems; BioTek Synergy 4 plate reader; Cary400 and Nanodrop spectrophotometers; crystallization incubators and Leica optical microscope; electrophoresis systems including custom preparative PAGE; BioRad Sequi-Gen GT sequencing gel systems; pH meter, balances, PCR thermocycler, microcentrifuges; chillers, refrigerators, -20 and -80 ˚C freezers).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific instruments, their uses (e.g., RNA transcription, protein purification, crystallization), and any specialized custom equipment. Demonstrate that necessary instrumentation for planned assays and analyses is on-site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lowen Laboratory — Equipment availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe equipment in collaborator/co-sponsor lab relevant to cell/molecular biology and virology experiments (examples: laminar flow hoods, CO2 incubators, inverted phase contrast microscope, microcentrifuges, electrophoresis systems, bacterial culture shaker/incubator, liquid nitrogen tank, -80 ˚C freezer, BioRad ChemiDoc imager, DNA thermal cyclers, BioRad real-time PCR instruments (384-well), droplet digital PCR (BioRad QX200); access to electroporation devices, Zeiss fluorescent microscope, Becton Dickinson FACS Calibur, ultracentrifuge and darkroom facilities nearby).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize availability of cell-based assay equipment, imaging, flow cytometry, and advanced PCR/digital PCR instrumentation relevant to the proposed cell infection/assay work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Shared Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: List shared departmental instrumentation that supports specialized studies (e.g., Phoenix nanoliter dispensing crystallization robot, Formulator liquid handling robot, Rigaku MicroMax007HF X-ray generator with ACTOR mounting robot, Varimax-HF optics, Saturn 944+ CCD detector, Oxford Cryosystem X-Stream system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate that shared equipment is housed in dedicated departmental space adjacent to labs, and provide context that these resources support multiple structural biology groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emory Core Facilities (ECBDC, HDX-MS, EIGC, ECGC) — access and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe core facilities to be used and their specific instruments (examples: ECBDC FortéBIO OctetRED384 BLI instrument for label-free molecular interaction analysis; HDX-MS core with ACQUITY UPLC System with HDX Manager and Waters Q-TOF Premier mass spectrometer and software (Masslynx 4.1, PLGS 3.0, Dynamix 3.2); EIGC Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer for ribosomal RNA analysis; ECGC GE Biacore X-100 SPR and Malvern/MicroCal Auto-iTC200 calorimeter). Mention physical location/proximity and that instruments are maintained under service agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide URLs or references for cores, note proximity (minutes/walking), describe core capabilities and any operational details (e.g., autosampler capacity, max resolution, software used), and indicate availability (service agreements, attached letters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) — required fields and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the Senior/Key Person Profile with required fields (e.g., Prefix, First Name*, Last Name*, Position/Title*, Organization Name*, Department, Street1*, City*, State*, Country*, Zip/Postal Code*, Phone Number*, E-Mail*, Project Role*: PD/PI for the PD/PI profile). Include attachments: Biographical Sketch (Attach Biographical Sketch*), Current & Pending Support, and tracking/funding opportunity identifiers (e.g., Tracking Number, Funding Opportunity Number, Received Date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the form fields exactly (asterisked items are required). Attach the biosketch PDF and current & pending support files as specified. Provide accurate contact and credential information (eRA Commons username, credential) and ensure Project Role is set appropriately (PD/PI for the application lead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to the specified format and five-page limit for each biosketch. Use the section headings A–D as organized below and include required subcomponents (education/training table, personal statement, positions and honors, contributions to science, scholastic performance where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A. Personal Statement — a concise narrative describing the individual's role in the proposed project, the goals of the proposed work for the applicant (e.g., obtaining extramural funding to support Ph.D. thesis research), how the fellowship will enhance technical and professional training, and career objectives (e.g., path to independent research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed project fits the applicant's training goals, relevant prior experience, specific skills to be gained, intended professional development activities (conferences, presentations, publications), and mentoring environment. Use the personal statement to justify suitability and training benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch B. Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: B. Positions and Honors — list activity/occupation with start and end dates (mm/yy), field, institution/company, and supervisor/employer. Include academic and professional honors with criteria when relevant (examples: HOPE Scholarship eligibility criteria, Dean's List GPA thresholds, honor societies with selection criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a chronological listing of positions and employment, and enumerate honors/awards with brief explanatory notes where appropriate (e.g., eligibility/selection criteria). Use this to demonstrate trajectory and recognition relevant to the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch C. Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: C. Contributions to Science — provide concise descriptions of up to several (illustrative) contributions (e.g., 'Regulation of 2’-5’-oligoadenylate synthetase 1 (OAS1) by double-stranded RNA'), describe the significance/impact of the work, the applicant's role in the work (e.g., developed assays, performed experiments, wrote manuscript), and cite representative publications (with journal citations and PMCID where available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each contribution include a short narrative of the findings/importance, the applicant's specific contributions/leadership, and 1–3 representative citations. Make clear independent contributions (e.g., co-first author) and downstream applications or presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch D. Scholastic Performance / Education/Training table
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Scholastic Performance — provide an education/training table listing institution and location, degree (if applicable), start date MM/YYYY, completion date MM/YYYY, and field of study. Include relevant course lists, grades, and GPA information (example: undergraduate and graduate course listings with grades and cumulative GPA; explanation of grading scale if needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include grade listings for coursework relevant to training background when requested. State GPA and any grading-scale clarifications (e.g., what 'A' equals numerically), and mark Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory courses when relevant. Keep this within the overall five-page biosketch limit.
